content: Indoor turn-by-turn differs from driving guidance only in complexity, not structure: instruction = distance travelled + direction change + named landmark. The standard indoor instruction grammar across vendors is distance to next manoeuvre, turn classification (left/right/straight/u-turn), an explicit floor-change instruction naming stairs or lift, and a remaining-distance/ETA readout. Navigine adds that routes should prefer suitable elevators, entrances and hallways. Ariadne adds that the accessible route should name the specific lift and ramp it uses and warn when the accessible route is materially longer or a lift is out of service. Academic work (Marciniak et al., MDPI Applied Sciences 14(22):10252, 2024) confirms indoor turn instructions are generated from route geometry by grouping same-floor nodes into legs and classifying bearing changes, which matches the pure-function design planned for this project.
